A.do: Use for raw anchor semantics and explicit URLs.
A.dont: Do not use for session event actions.
A.accessibility: Provide descriptive link text and a valid href.

Alert.summary: A status message that communicates important feedback.
Alert.do: Use a meaningful tone and concise message.
Alert.dont: Do not encode critical state only through color.
Alert.accessibility: Render an appropriate status or alert role.

Badge.dont: Do not use badges as the only explanation of an action.
Badge.accessibility: Ensure the surrounding context explains the label.

Button.do: Use an action verb and explicit loading/disabled state.
Button.dont: Do not use a button for navigation.
Button.accessibility: Use an accessible name and preserve keyboard focus.

Card.do: Use for one coherent content group.
Card.dont: Do not nest cards without a clear hierarchy.
Card.accessibility: Use headings and landmarks inside when needed.

Container.do: Use to constrain reading and layout width.
Container.dont: Do not use fixed widths that block zoom.
Container.accessibility: Preserve logical reading order and reflow.

Div.do: Use when no more specific semantic element fits.
Div.dont: Do not use divs as interactive controls.
Div.accessibility: Prefer a semantic landmark or heading where applicable.

Flex.do: Use for directional alignment and spacing.
Flex.dont: Do not use layout CSS to communicate document hierarchy.
Flex.accessibility: Keep DOM order meaningful independent of visual order.

Form.summary: Semantic form grouping and submission surface.
Form.do: Pair controls with labels and validation feedback.
Form.dont: Do not rely on placeholders as labels.
Form.accessibility: Expose labels, errors, required state, and keyboard flow.

Grid.do: Use for related items that need columns and rows.
Grid.dont: Do not create horizontal overflow at zoom.
Grid.accessibility: Preserve source order and responsive reflow.

Heading.dont: Do not choose levels only for visual size.
Heading.accessibility: Keep heading levels ordered and descriptive.

Input.do: Declare type, name, label, and validation behavior.
Input.dont: Do not expose sensitive input as plain text.
Input.accessibility: Associate a visible label and error/help text.

Label.summary: Visible name for a form control.
Label.do: Use one clear label per control.
Label.dont: Do not use placeholder text as the label.
Label.accessibility: Associate the label with the native control.

Page.do: Use one primary page landmark per route.
Page.dont: Do not nest competing main landmarks.
Page.accessibility: Provide a descriptive page heading and landmark.

Stack.dont: Do not encode meaning only through spacing.
Stack.accessibility: Keep content order and reading flow intact.

Text.do: Use for readable content with sufficient contrast.
Text.dont: Do not use text styling as a substitute for semantics.
Text.accessibility: Preserve readable contrast, zoom, and line length.
